events.title: FOMC September decision (first Warsh SEP/dot plot)
events.why_it_matters: Funds rate is 3.50–3.75%; Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech has lifted September 25bp hike odds to roughly 55–65%, making this the cycle's highest-stakes meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Hold vs 25bp hike, the new SEP/dots, and whether Warsh treats July's payroll drop as noise versus a labor break.

events.title: US August employment report
events.why_it_matters: July payrolls fell 23k (first negative print of the cycle) even as unemployment eased to 4.1%; August is the last jobs print before the Warsh FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Whether payrolls rebound or print a second decline, plus unemployment, wages, and revisions that could swing hike odds.

events.title: US August CPI
events.why_it_matters: July CPI was +0.1% m/m / +3.4% y/y (core +0.2% / +2.5%); Warsh has called inflation 'concerning' with PCE still near 3.7%, so a hot August print would all but lock a September hike.
events.what_to_watch: Core goods/services split and energy pass-through from the Iran/Hormuz shock versus any disinflation that would support a hold.

events.title: US August PPI
events.why_it_matters: Producer prices the day before CPI will show whether energy, tariffs, and AI-capex goods inflation are still feeding into consumer prices.
events.what_to_watch: Core PPI and pipeline energy/goods components as a sneak preview of the Sep 11 CPI risk.

events.title: JOLTS job openings (July)
events.why_it_matters: June openings were 7.36 million (4.4% rate); consensus is ~7.33 million — a further drop would reinforce the July payroll shock ahead of Friday's jobs report.
events.what_to_watch: Openings, quits, and the vacancies-to-unemployed ratio as the first labor-market tell of the week.

events.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (August)
events.why_it_matters: July ISM manufacturing was 55.6 (seventh expansion month); consensus ~55.2 — still a growth signal that sits awkwardly next to a possible Fed hike.
events.what_to_watch: New orders, prices paid, and employment sub-indices for tariff/energy cost pressure.

events.title: ECB rate decision (Berlin)
events.why_it_matters: Deposit rate is 2.25% after a June hike and a July hold; markets now price an ~80–86% chance of another 25bp hike to 2.50% on energy-driven inflation — a hawkish reset versus last scan's cut watch.
events.what_to_watch: 25bp hike vs hold, updated staff projections, and any signal that oil/Hormuz keeps the ECB in a tightening bias.

events.title: Dell Q2 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: AI-server bellwether reports after the close; Q1 AI-optimized servers were $16.1B with a $51.3B backlog, and Q2 guide is ~$44–45B revenue / ~$4.80 adj. EPS.
events.what_to_watch: AI server shipments vs backlog, memory-constraint commentary, margins, and any FY2027 AI-server guide change around the ~$60B target.

events.title: Broadcom Q3 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Next AI-chip test after Nvidia's blowout; Street is ~$3.21–$3.24 EPS and ~$29.2–$29.5B revenue, with AI semis guided ~$16B (>200% y/y) and FY26 AI revenue $56B.
events.what_to_watch: AI semiconductor beat/guide, custom-ASIC customer concentration, and whether FY27 >$100B AI target is reiterated.

events.title: Nvidia Q2 FY2027 blowout (still in play)
events.why_it_matters: Revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), data center $89.0B, net income $59.7B, Q3 guide $108B ±2% — the AI capex supercycle remains the market's core bull case.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Broadcom/Dell confirm the same demand, and if supply/memory bottlenecks cap the FY28 ~70% growth claim.

events.title: Apple 'Surprise and Shine' iPhone 18 event
events.why_it_matters: First hardware event under new CEO John Ternus; expected iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and a rumored first foldable, with base iPhone 18 reportedly slipped to spring 2027.
events.what_to_watch: Foldable confirmation, pricing, A20/2nm claims, and pre-order timing around Sep 11–18.

events.title: John Ternus becomes Apple CEO
events.why_it_matters: Tim Cook's succession is effective today; hardware-engineer Ternus now owns the product cycle, China risk, and AI-on-device narrative into next week's event.
events.what_to_watch: Any day-one strategy comments and whether the Sep 9 event is used to reset the hardware roadmap.

events.title: SHEIN Hong Kong IPO debut
events.why_it_matters: Priced at HK$48.56, raising ~US$1.7B at ~US$26.5B value (vs ~$100B 2022 peak); shares slid as much as ~10% on debut amid growth, de minimis, and forced-labor overhangs.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the stock stabilizes and if the weak debut chills other China/consumer IPOs.

events.title: Canada dollar-for-dollar tariffs take effect
events.why_it_matters: After talks collapsed Aug 21, Ottawa matches US 50% tariffs on ~$20–28B of US goods (steel, furniture, apparel, dairy, electronics) from 12:01 a.m. EDT Sep 8; Carney called it a trade 'war'.
events.what_to_watch: Last-minute delay/deal, pass-through into US consumer prices, and auto/steel/aluminum spillover.

events.title: Section 232 drone/UAS tariffs effective
events.why_it_matters: Proclamation 11055 (Aug 13) imposes 100% duties on larger/thermal UAS and 25% on smaller drones from 12:01 a.m. ET Sep 3, aimed at China supply chains with allied 10–15% caps.
events.what_to_watch: Import-price spikes, China retaliation risk, and any onshoring/Blue UAS exemptions that mute the hit.

events.title: Congress FY2027 CR / shutdown sprint
events.why_it_matters: FY2026 funding lapses Sep 30; House CR (H.R. 9770) and a Senate CR through early December still need reconciliation in a GOP September sprint — shutdown is not base case but is the live fiscal risk.
events.what_to_watch: Chamber differences on duration/riders and whether defense/immigration fights delay a CR into late September.

events.title: US national debt crossed $40 trillion
events.why_it_matters: Gross debt hit ~$40.05T on Aug 18, months earlier than many forecasts; ceiling is $41.1T (no September X-date) but term-premium/fiscal worries remain live into the FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Treasury auction demand, long-end yields, and any Warsh/Treasury public split on deficits vs inflation.

events.title: Jackson Hole: Warsh hawkish debut
events.why_it_matters: New Chair Warsh called inflation concerning, said the Fed has 'work to do,' and stayed quiet on cuts — the speech that re-priced September from hold to a coin-flip/lean-hike.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Sep 4 jobs and Sep 11 CPI validate or unwind that hawkish re-pricing before Sep 16.

events.title: China NBS manufacturing PMI 49.8
events.why_it_matters: Official factory PMI rose to 49.8 from 49.2 but stayed in contraction a second month; non-manufacturing 49.0 and composite 49.5 keep pressure on incremental Beijing support.
events.what_to_watch: Whether production/new-orders sub-50 relapse forces a larger PBoC/fiscal step beyond targeted tools.

events.title: China 800bn yuan policy financing tool opens
events.why_it_matters: Project applications began for an ~800bn yuan (~$119B) policy-based financing tool plus a smaller ultra-long bond consumer package — incremental, not bazooka, stimulus.
events.what_to_watch: Disbursement speed vs rollout lags; any upgrade from 'targeted' to broad easing if PMI stays sub-50.

events.title: South Korea August chip/export boom
events.why_it_matters: MOTIR data: August semiconductor exports $46.65B (+209% y/y); total exports $98.25B (+68.7%) and surplus $34.75B — hard confirmation of the AI hardware cycle outside the US.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the surge holds into September and if BOK tightening starts to bite domestic demand.

events.title: Bank of Korea hikes to 3.00%
events.why_it_matters: Rare back-to-back 25bp hikes took the base rate to 3.00% as GDP was revised to 3.3% on chip/AI exports; no September meeting, next likely October.
events.what_to_watch: Won stability, household-debt/housing stress, and whether the median path toward ~3.25% is confirmed.

events.title: Japan–Korea FX intervention coordination
events.why_it_matters: Tokyo and Seoul pledged close FX coordination after a rare intervention as yen/won weakness met oil-driven inflation — a live G10/EM FX risk into BoJ Sep 17–18 (just beyond this window).
events.what_to_watch: Further yen/won slides on oil spikes and whether intervention talk returns before the BoJ meeting.

events.title: SCO summit in Bishkek (Xi, Putin, Modi, Pezeshkian)
events.why_it_matters: 26th SCO heads-of-state summit closes today with a Bishkek Declaration; side meetings cover energy (Power of Siberia 2), Ukraine, and West Asia/Iran — a non-Western diplomatic counterweight to Washington.
events.what_to_watch: Any concrete energy, de-dollarization, or Iran-mediation language beyond communiqué boilerplate.

events.title: US–Iran war flare: Hormuz strikes, oil bid
events.why_it_matters: Weekend US strikes on Larak Island mine launchers and Iranian missiles at Jordan bases broke a month-long lull; Brent >$91 / WTI ~$86–87 on Sep 1 as Hormuz traffic stays impaired — the dominant energy tail risk.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the June Islamabad MOU holds, further shipping attacks, and any move back toward $100–120 if the Strait tightens again.

events.title: OPEC+ core-group meeting (post-September hike)
events.why_it_matters: The Aug 2 decision put +188k bpd in place for September (completing the 2023 voluntary-cut rollback); Sep 6 is the next chance to pause Q4 hikes while ~2M bpd of older cuts remain.
events.what_to_watch: Q4 pause vs another increment, and any statement on Iran/Hormuz disruptions versus spare capacity.

events.title: Ukraine–Russia talks window (unconfirmed)
events.why_it_matters: Zelenskyy aide Budanov said Sep talks with possible US participation could revive a process stalled since Feb when Washington pivoted to Iran; the Kremlin says it has no such information.
events.what_to_watch: Any confirmed date/venue and whether territorial red lines (Donetsk vs current line of contact) actually move.

events.title: SEMICON Taiwan 2026
events.why_it_matters: Largest chip-equipment gathering of the month (1,300+ exhibitors) focused on AI packaging, CPO/silicon photonics, and power — a real-time read on the bottleneck after Nvidia's guide.
events.what_to_watch: TSMC/OSAT capacity comments, advanced-packaging lead times, and any Taiwan-risk or power-constraint flags.

events.title: Treasury Operation Economic Outcast (Iran sectoral sanctions)
events.why_it_matters: OFAC added five EO 13902 sectoral determinations (digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, shipping), designated ~60 persons/vessels, and suspended Iran general licenses with a wind-down through Sep 8—secondary-sanctions risk for banks, crypto, and shadow-fleet oil.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Sep 8 license expiry forces more de-risking of Iran oil/crypto rails and whether follow-on designations hit UAE/HK/China intermediaries.

events.title: EO declaring national emergency on US bulk-power system
events.why_it_matters: IEEPA emergency lets DOE prohibit acquisition/import/install of foreign-produced grid equipment (transformers, inverters, BESS, ICS) from covered foreign entities, with implementing rules due within 120 days—direct hit to China-linked electrical gear as AI data-center load surges.
events.what_to_watch: DOE covered-entity list, pre-qualification of vendors, and any forced isolation/replacement of already-installed Chinese inverters and transformers.

events.title: SEC proposes Regulation Crypto Assets
events.why_it_matters: Creates tailored Securities Act exemptions (startup up to $5M; fundraising up to $75M/12 months) plus a path to end investment-contract status—first comprehensive US crypto offering regime of the cycle.
events.what_to_watch: 60-day comment period (~through Oct 20) and whether the safe harbor is seen as workable for token issuers and exchanges.

events.title: BIS black-mass and tungsten scrap domestic-allocation order effective
events.why_it_matters: One-year DPA/DPAS temporary final rule requires 100% of monthly US sales of lithium-ion black mass and tungsten waste/scrap to stay with US persons, tightening battery-recycling and defense-metal supply.
events.what_to_watch: BIS exception grants for foreign processing-and-return and any expansion to other critical minerals.

events.title: Meta ~$17B multistate youth-safety settlement
events.why_it_matters: Largest Big Tech state consumer settlement (~$12B base, up to ~$17B) plus mandatory under-18 time limits, night blocks, and an independent auditor—cash and product constraints on Instagram/Facebook engagement.
events.what_to_watch: Court approval in NDCA, copycat terms for TikTok/Snap/YouTube that could trigger the upside payment, and any engagement/ad-load hit in teen cohorts.

events.title: China holds 1Y/5Y LPR unchanged (15th month)
events.why_it_matters: PBOC left 1Y LPR at 3.0% and 5Y at 3.5% despite factory PMI still in contraction, confirming a fiscal-not-rate easing bias.
events.what_to_watch: Any RRR or policy-rate cut if September data stay weak; 5Y LPR is the mortgage benchmark.

events.title: US initial jobless claims (week ending Aug 29)
events.why_it_matters: First high-frequency labor print after July's −23k payrolls and ahead of Friday's August employment report.
events.what_to_watch: A sustained rise in claims would undercut the Warsh hike case; a drop would reinforce it.

events.title: University of Michigan sentiment (September preliminary)
events.why_it_matters: Drops the same morning as August CPI; 1-year and 5–10 year inflation expectations are the component Warsh will cite if they re-accelerate with oil >$91.
events.what_to_watch: Inflation-expectations subcomponent, not the headline sentiment index.

events.title: Existing home sales (August)
events.why_it_matters: July sales were 4.06M SAAR with a ~4.6-month supply; August is a rate-sensitive housing check the day of PPI and 30-year Treasury reopenings.
events.what_to_watch: Median price, inventory months, and pending-sales follow-through if mortgage rates stay elevated into FOMC.

events.title: US 10-year and 30-year Treasury reopenings
events.why_it_matters: Long-end supply (~$39B 10s / ~$22B 30s, subject to confirmation) hits into PPI/CPI week with $40T debt and hike-odds already elevated.
events.what_to_watch: Tail ratios, dealer awards, and whether 30-year bid-to-cover weakens term premium into the Warsh FOMC.

events.title: Oracle Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Last major cloud/AI-infrastructure print before the Warsh FOMC; remaining-performance-obligation and OCI capacity commentary will confirm or fade the Nvidia/Broadcom capex story.
events.what_to_watch: OCI growth, RPO, capex, and any Stargate/large-training-cluster updates.

top_risks: Warsh Fed 25bp hike on Sep 16 if Aug jobs rebound and/or Aug CPI re-accelerates — hike odds already ~55–65%.
US–Iran/Hormuz re-escalation driving oil back toward $100–120 and importing inflation into US/EU/BoJ policy.
Canada–US tariff war going live Sep 8 with no deal, hitting autos, metals, consumer goods, and inflation prints.
Policy collision: weak labor (July −23k) versus hawkish Warsh/ECB/BOK tightening into an energy shock.
China official PMI stuck sub-50 while stimulus stays incremental, dragging global industrials/materials.
top_opportunities: Dell today and Broadcom tomorrow confirming Nvidia's AI capex supercycle (the market's still-dominant bull pillar).
Soft Aug jobs (Sep 4) and/or cool CPI (Sep 11) that unwind hike odds and rally duration/risk.
Iran de-escalation back toward the June MOU, easing the oil risk premium from ~$91 Brent.
Korea's $46.7B chip-export print plus SEMICON Taiwan as fundamental support for the hardware complex.
Apple foldable/iPhone 18 Pro event (Sep 9) if Ternus delivers a cleaner hardware cycle than feared.
summary: September opens with elevated uncertainty: Warsh's first FOMC (Sep 15–16) is a live hike call (~55–65%) gated by Friday's jobs report and Sep 11 CPI, while a fresh US–Iran flare has oil back above $91 rather than the $120 spike of earlier in the war. Canada's matching tariffs hit Sep 8 and the ECB is now a hike risk (not a cut). The offset is still AI: Nvidia's $96B quarter is unconfirmed by Dell (today) and Broadcom (tomorrow), with Korea chip exports exploding. China remains in manufacturing contraction with only targeted easing.

catcher.coverage_assessment: Primary was strong on the Warsh FOMC path, mega-cap AI earnings, Canada/232 tariffs, the FY2027 CR, and the US–Iran oil flare. It was blind on agency/executive actions (Treasury Iran sectorals, bulk-power IEEPA EO, SEC crypto proposal, BIS critical-minerals allocation) and on second-tier US data (ISM Services, claims, UMich expectations, housing, long-end auctions).
catcher.biggest_gap: Treasury Operation Economic Outcast (Aug 24): primary tracked Hormuz strikes and the oil bid but missed the largest OFAC/Treasury campaign of the window, including five new Iran sectoral determinations and a Sep 8 general-license wind-down.
